name_en: Finite difference method for ordinary differential equations (method-family label)
canonical_name: finite-difference numerical treatment of ODEs (exact theorem open)
literal_source_claim_en: A numerical method for ordinary differential equations.
statement_blocker: The catalog names a numerical method family but supplies no ODE problem, grid, stencil or recurrence, discrete solution, hypotheses, or conclusion. It does not choose derivative approximation, scheme solvability, consistency, order, zero- or absolute-stability, convergence, or an error bound, and it does not distinguish initial-value from boundary-value results. Selecting Euler or any other familiar theorem would invent missing mathematics; importing the separate THM-M-1465 PDE scope would substitute another target.
domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix an initial- or boundary-value ODE, scalar or vector state space, time domain, vector field and data, exact-solution notion, discrete grid and state carrier, arithmetic model, and all universes and typeclass assumptions.
conclusion: Open: the repository names a numerical-method family but states no consistency, order, stability, convergence, solvability, or local/global error proposition.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; step-size, grid, endpoint, exact-solution, discrete-solvability, regularity, norm, and time-horizon boundary cases remain statement decisions.
candidate_scope_not_credited: consistency and local truncation error of a selected derivative stencil or one-step method
convergence or a global error bound for forward or backward Euler on a selected ODE initial-value problem
zero-stability plus consistency implying convergence for a source-selected linear multistep method
solvability, stability, convergence, or error of a finite-difference discretization of a selected ODE boundary-value problem
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: zero, negative, variable, or overly large step size; empty or singleton grids; and a final endpoint not aligned with the mesh
zero-dimensional state, constant or zero vector fields, equilibria, and zero-length time intervals
non-Lipschitz fields, nonunique or blowing-up exact solutions, and trajectories reaching the ODE-domain boundary
singular implicit updates or boundary matrices, inconsistent data, and nonunique discrete solutions
local versus global error, finite versus infinite time horizon, norm and constant uniformity, and order-zero or exact-polynomial cases
exact-real versus floating-point arithmetic, roundoff, adaptive or nonuniform grids, and startup values for multistep schemes
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1394 shooting, THM-M-1396 Runge-Kutta, THM-M-1397 Adams, THM-M-1398 stiff equations, or THM-M-1399 backward differentiation without an exact source identity
the algebraic forward-difference operator or a derivative-quotient limit presented as a numerical ODE theorem
a generic Taylor remainder or continuous approximate-trajectory estimate without a checked bridge to a selected discrete scheme
a scalar, linear, autonomous, one-step, uniformly spaced, or finite-horizon special case substituted for an unselected general root
a structure or hypothesis that stores the exact solution, discrete solution, convergence, stability, or requested error bound as data
a computed trajectory, sampled error table, floating-point experiment, plot, solver output, oracle, or unchecked certificate
the untrusted catalog label verified as human-source or Lean kernel evidence

foundation_profile: Lean 4 dependent type theory is intended; classical logic, choice, real-analysis completeness, finite-dimensional coordinate identifications, ODE existence and uniqueness, and limit principles remain open because no proposition is selected
tcb_profile: Lean kernel 4.29.0 and pinned mathlib are the intended base; exact minimal imports, scheme implementation, terminal declarations, transitive dependency closure, executables, and trust policy remain open
computation_profile: No floating-point solver, native numerical experiment, plot, sampled convergence table, oracle, or unchecked error certificate is credited; the eventual theorem must specify whether its discrete arithmetic is abstract exact arithmetic or a separately certified floating-point model
formal_system: Lean 4 + pinned mathlib under the rev-5.6 adapter

freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on source or target correction, theorem-family or neighbor-ownership decision, ODE, state, domain, data, solution, regularity, grid, step, stencil, recurrence, arithmetic, consistency, stability, convergence, error, norm, quantifier, constant, or boundary choice, canonical Lean target, toolchain or dependency pin, assurance profile, validator, or any owned artifact change; independent review and master acceptance remain open.

H5 classifies the supplied finite-difference method label and ODE numerical-method gloss as not yet a stable proposition; it does not refute a reviewed finite-difference theorem. The modern source lead and adjacent pinned APIs supply discovery evidence only. No canonical mathematical or Lean proposition, H0, M0, R0, accepted proof state, audit completion, theorem completion, or master acceptance is claimed.
